entries.title: Católicos de Chicago rinden homenaje a quienes murieron bajo custodia de ICE con cruces de madera
entries.summary: <p>Armados con 104 cruces, cada una adornada con un nombre individual, líderes católicos y trabajadores sindicalizados se reunieron el jueves en una iglesia del centro para presentar una nueva instalación destinada a honrar a las víctimas de las agresivas prácticas migratorias y a impulsar una reforma.</p><p>La instalación conmemora a cada persona que ha muerto bajo custodia migratoria o durante operativos migratorios desde 2020, pintando sus nombres en una cruz. Las cruces estarán en la Catedral del Santo Nombre y luego se trasladarán a distintas parroquias del área de Chicago, incluyendo Catholic Theological Union en Hyde Park y Sta. Sabina en Auburn Gresham.</p><p>El reverendo Brendan Curran, cofundador de Sacerdotes por la Justicia para los Inmigrantes, dijo que el proyecto tiene dos objetivos: honrar a quienes han muerto y trabajar por un mejor trato para los inmigrantes, lo que incluye apoyar a candidatos políticos que respalden los derechos de los inmigrantes.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-ce0000" name="module-ce0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>“Este lado de esta exhibición es una indicación muy clara de que nuestro sistema está roto, y tenemos que hacer algo mejor que esto para el futuro de este país”, dijo Curran.</p><p>Animó a los católicos y a otros defensores de los inmigrantes a votar en las elecciones legislativas de noviembre y a presionar a los miembros del Congreso para restablecer el Estatus de Protección Temporal (TPS) para los inmigrantes haitianos.</p><p>Curran también pidió apoyo para el proyecto de ley Drain ICE Act, presentado en febrero, que retiraría $75 mil millones en fondos para el Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE) y otros sistemas federales de control migratorio.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" entries.title: 15 planes violated temporary flight restriction in 'highly anomalous' spike during Trump's Medinah visit
entries.summary: <p>Fifteen civilian planes violated a temporary flight restriction that was in place on Sunday during President Trump's nine-hour trip to Illinois, with flares being deployed at two planes who did not initially respond to F-16 military jets flying alongside their wings.</p><p>The North American Aerospace Defense Command, or NORAD, told the Chicago Sun-Times the violations marked a "highly anomalous and significant spike for a single weekend." </p><p>Trump landed at O'Hare Airport at 9:40 a.m. to attend the<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/09/27/trump-appears-sunday-at-the-presidents-cup-golf-tournament-in-suburban-medinah" > Presidents Cup golf tournament</a> in northwest suburban Medinah. Air Force One was wheeled up at O'Hare at 6:40 p.m. During that time, NORAD put in place a VIP temporary flight restriction over the Chicago area. </p><p>NORAD says 15 general aviation aircraft violated the temporary flight restriction. NORAD fighter aircraft, including F-16s, were deployed as a "standard precautionary measure to ensure airspace security and establish visual contact with the unresponsive aircraft," NORAD said in a statement.</p><p>In 10 of those instances, fighter aircraft performed tactical intercepts to get the attention of the pilots. During two of those intercepts, flares were dispensed which may have been visible to the public. Those flares were used to ensure pilots saw the NORAD aircraft and to communicate with the pilots, the agency said.</p><p>"All 15 situations were safely resolved with the aircraft escorted out of the restricted airspace," NORAD said. </p><p>Still, the military organization that is jointly operated by the United States and Canada, says the number of violations was unusual and that several factors may have contributed to that spike. NORAD said there has been a national average of between 40 and 50 restricted air space violations per month since early 2026, resulting in upwards of nine intercepts and five instances where flares were used. </p><p>"This localized surge was likely driven by a combination of factors, including the infrequency of NORAD-enforced restrictions in the Chicago airspace, pilots operating on routinely familiar but temporarily restricted flight paths, and a critical gap in pre-flight planning regarding active FAA Notices to Air Missions (NOTAMs)," Major Jennie Derenzis of NORAD's media division said in an email. "Additionally, a shift in the TFR’s active schedule may have also caught multiple aviators off guard, highlighting the critical importance of rigorous pre-flight planning and real-time monitoring of active FAA Notices to Air Missions (NOTAMs)."</p><p>Trump's public schedule, released on Saturday, did not list a time of departure from the Chicago area. But according to pool reports, there was an original expectation of being back in Washington after 5 p.m. Eastern time. Trump instead landed at Joint Base Andrews at 9:10 p.m </p><p>During flight restrictions, pilots are expected to pay attention to NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions), which are filed with aviation authorities to notify pilots about airspace restrictions and hazards. During an interception, two fighters approach the plane, with pilots usually only seeing one, <a class="Link" href="https://www.norad.mil/General-Aviation/" target="_blank" >according to NORAD</a>. The intent is to identify the plane and try to figure out why it's in restricted space and encourage them to communicate with air traffic controllers. The fighter jets can also help escort the plane out of the airspace. If that doesn't work, flares are deployed to get the attention of the pilot. </p><p> </p><p>The Federal Aviation Administration on Monday said it investigates all flight restriction violations and takes "appropriate action." The agency said it does not discuss open investigations and referred questions to the U.S. Northern Command and the U.S. Secret Service. The agency said sanctions range from warnings to license suspensions or revocations, based on the circumstances of the violation.</p><p>Sunday marked Trump's first visit to Illinois during his second presidency. He last came to Chicago in July 2024 during a combative interview at the National Association of Black Journalists conference, where he <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2024/07/31/donald-trump-nabj-q-a-kamala-harris-chicago-conference-black-journalists" target="_blank" >questioned the racial identity of Vice President Kamala Harris</a> and lambasted a moderator’s question about derogatory statements he has made toward the Black community.</p>

entries.title: City Council faction draws line in sand in preelection budget battle with Mayor Brandon Johnson
entries.summary: <p>The 29-member City Council coalition that rejected Mayor Brandon Johnson’s corporate head tax on Monday laid the ground rules for the pre-election budget debate with three boundary lines: no property tax, no “head tax or tax on job growth” and no counting on money from Springfield not yet approved.</p><p>With an $882.4 million shortfall looming less than five months before the mayoral election, Johnson has drawn his own line in the sand. He is staking his uphill battle for re-election on a promise to “tax the rich.” </p><p>The mayor has also pointedly refused to rule out a pre-election property tax hike — even after his proposed $300 million property tax increase was unanimously rejected by the City Council nearly two years ago.</p><p>Against that backdrop, the parameters established by the opposition coalition of alderpersons that Johnson likes to call the “Corporate Caucus” appear to put the mayor and Council on a collision course that could make last year’s budget stalemate look tame by comparison.</p><p>The group that calls itself the Budget Accountability Coalition said in a letter to Johnson Monday that its 29 members “recognize spending cuts alone may not responsibly erase the entire deficit.”</p><p>But the coalition is prepared to consider what it calls “locally-controlled revenue options” only after “meaningful recurring savings are on the table.” </p><p>The group argued that any effort to generate new revenue must begin with “money already owed to the city: collecting it, recovering our costs and modernizing existing revenue where it makes sense.”</p><p>“Reduce the cost of government. Protect essential services. Collecting what is already owed. Determine the truly remaining structural deficit. Then and only then decide what new revenue, if any, is truly necessary,” the letter states.</p><p>“Our position is plain: No property tax increase. No head tax or tax on job growth. No counting on Springfield money that has not been approved. Within those bounds, we stand ready to work with you.”</p><p>Last year, an emboldened City Council <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/12/20/chicago-budget-veto-brandon-johnson-alternate-head-tax" >seized control </a>over the budget process long control by the mayor in a way not seen since the 1980s power struggled known as “Council Wars” that saw 29-mostly white alderpersons thwart then-Mayor Harold Washington’s every move.</p><p>The same 29-member coalition that wrote Monday’s letter rejected Johnson's corporate head tax and approved an alternative revenue package with several major elements that Johnson vehemently opposed and has either been unwilling or unable to implement.</p><p>The Council lifted the Chicago ban on video gambling terminals, but the Johnson administration has yet to license a single <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/casinos-gambling/2026/06/19/chicago-video-gambling-machines-vgt-bars-restaurants" >video gambling terminal </a>even though the Illinois Gaming Board has licensed 65 Chicago applicants. And a plan to sell nearly $1 billion in outstanding city debt collapsed after a lack of interest from banks.</p><p>That left the city with an $85.1 million mid-year shortfall. Determined to avoid employee layoffs, Johnson refinanced up to $525 million in outstanding city debt and said he would use pandemic relief funds as a back-up. </p><p>Those are the kinds of short-term fixes that the opposition coalition is ruling out in the upcoming debate.</p><p>“One-time money must not paper over a permanent problem. Borrowing, refinancing, reserves and asset sales have no business underwriting operations,” the letter states. “A one-time expense does not justify a permanent tax. A program launched on temporary federal dollars should not quietly become a standing obligation of Chicago taxpayers.”</p><p>The mayor’s office said it welcomes “good faith engagement” by the Council and “all other stakeholders” heading into budget season. But the statement encouraged alderpersons to “come to the table not only with a list of what they will not support, but with concrete solutions” to eliminate the shortfall.</p><p>“We will not balance the budget on the backs of working people or by cutting critical services Chicagoans rely on,” the statement said.</p><p></p><p>Last week, the Johnson administration responded to a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/09/24/civic-committee-commercial-club-of-chicago-city-hall-financial-crisis-recommendations" >financial report </a>issued by an influential business group by claiming that the "real path forward for Chicago's long-term financial future is through sustainable progressive revenue."</p><p>Northwest Side Ald. Samantha Nugent (39th) argued that the $882.4 million shortfall in next year's budget would have been "much smaller" if Johnson had fully implemented the 2026 budget, instead of “sabotaging” the alternative spending plan.</p><p>"With this letter, we’re providing clarity. A budget that raises taxes before seeking cuts and efficiencies, or that relies on Springfield revenue that doesn’t exist, is a non-starter,” Nugent told the Sun-Times.</p><p>“We’re also being really clear on what we won’t support from last year’s proposals. Namely, a tax on jobs that penalizes businesses for hiring or cutting our advance pension payment or leaving uncollected debt on the table when collecting it would reduce the need for revenue elsewhere.”</p><p>Nugent was asked what good a letter providing “clarity” will do when Johnson has already drawn his own line in the sand by renewing his tax-the-rich mantra.</p><p>“The City Council is a co-equal branch of government. It’s up to us to pass the budget. And the lesson from the past year is, we can’t start with tax increases," Nugent said. "We need to begin by finding efficiencies and collecting more of the debt.” </p>

entries.title: Vikings trade QB J.J. McCarthy to Giants for a 2027 fifth-round draft pick
entries.summary: <p>The New York Giants acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 fifth-round pick on Monday, adding another young player at the most important position in football less than a week after learning Jaxson Dart would be out for at least the rest of the regular season because of a knee injury.</p><p>"We've been talking about it ever since, I think, Jaxson got hurt, that we would need to add a quarterback — quarterbacks," Giants coach John Harbaugh said. "We've been turning over every stone. This was an opportunity that kind of came up and able to finish the deal off."</p><p>McCarthy, the 10th pick in the 2024 draft, gets a change of scenery after losing the starting job in Minnesota to Kyler Murray and falling behind Carson Wentz on the depth chart. McCarthy started 10 games last season, completing 57.6% of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.</p><p>"Nothing about this changes the way I feel about J.J. or the hopes I have for him," said Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell, who had what he called an emotional 1-on-1 meeting with McCarthy about the trade. "I think it's a good opportunity in New York and, as I told him, I'll be pulling for him like crazy to see him go and do well and apply a lot of the things that we talked about in his period of time here."</p><p>McCarthy missed what would have been his rookie season after injuring his right knee. He was picked a year ahead of Dart, but each was born in 2003, with McCarthy being just four months older.</p><p>Long term, that sets up a fascinating situation for New York, with Dart, Jameis Winston and McCarthy all under contract for next season. For now, McCarthy joins in a reserve role to learn the offense, while Harbaugh reiterated that Winston will start again Sunday against Arizona after beating Tennessee despite not scoring a touchdown and having just 238 yards of offense.</p><p>By making this aggressive move, Harbaugh, general manager Joe Schoen and the Giants are doubling down on trying to contend now, even after losing Dart and linebacker Brian Burns to season-ending knee injuries.</p><p>"You need another quarterback, in our situation, and you want to go get the very best quarterback you could get, which is what we did," Harbaugh said. "Very talented player and is going to make us a stronger football team."</p><p>There is familial familiarity with McCarthy, who won the national title at Michigan in his final college season playing for John's younger brother Jim Harbaugh.</p><p>"He always had good things to say about J.J.," John Harbaugh said. "When Jim was there, that was a team I watched closely, so I've watched J.J. play a lot."</p><p>It is still possible the Giants bring in another quarterback, though they did not hold tryouts Monday, according to the league's transactions report. Jake Haener backed up Winston during the Titans game and figures to stick around on the practice squad, with either he or McCarthy serving in that role this weekend.</p><p>"You never know," Harbaugh said. "I would say all options are on the table."</p><p>For the Vikings, the trade served as yet another reminder of the quarterback carousel the franchise has continually found itself on. Murray and Wentz are set to be free agents next spring, so the organization will yet again be forced to make multiple decisions and evaluations about who to build around for next season and beyond. Murray became the ninth different starting quarterback since Kirk Cousins took the field at Green Bay on Oct. 29, 2023, and tore his Achilles tendon.</p><p>"A lot of the decisions that we make and that we're forced to make in football we have to make in a moment in time as opposed to hypotheticals in the future," GM Nolan Teasley said. "And so that's really reflective of this decision, that we think it's in the best interests of the Minnesota Vikings right now."</p><p>McCarthy was the fifth quarterback taken among the record six selected in the first 12 picks in the 2024 draft, when Caleb Williams went to the Bears, Jayden Daniels to Washington and Drake Maye to New England with the first three spots. Michael Penix was picked eighth by Atlanta, followed by McCarthy at No. 10 and Bo Nix to Denver at No. 12.</p><p>McCarthy lost only three games as the starter through high school and college, including a 27-1 record at Michigan on the way to the championship, but he came to the Vikings with minimal experience as a pro-style passer after being in Jim Harbaugh's run-heavy offense. The energy and toughness that helped McCarthy become a winner and a leader at the lower levels worked against him at times last season, with a tendency for recklessness and a pattern of inaccuracy that contributed to his disappointing debut.</p><p>"Sometimes things don't work out how you envisioned or how you planned or how you hoped, and that doesn't change the intent," O'Connell said. "That doesn't change the work that got put into it by J.J. himself and what he's meant within this building since the time we first got him. So, I believe in the collective work that was put in, and I believe in J.J. and the intent and the work that he put in. This is just where we are."</p>

entries.title: Bears’ inactives vs. Eagles: K Cairo Santos, CB Tyrique Stevenson good to go
entries.summary: <p>Other than the massive absence of starting quarterback Caleb Williams, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a> go into their game Monday night against the Eagles relatively healthy.</p><p>Williams was the only player made inactive because of an injury, and third-stringer Case Keenum has been working with the starting offense leading up to kickoff. Tyson Bagent, who cleared concussion protocol Sunday, will be active as Keenum's backup.</p><p>Two injury concerns for the Bears cleared up late in the week: Kicker Cairo Santos (right hip) and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson (hamstring) are active and expected to play. Bears coach Ben Johnson said the team was surprised by Stevenson's progress after initially implying he'd probably be out this week.</p><p>Bears running backs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/26/bears-need-rushing-attack-to-lead-way-against-eagles-just-like-last-season" >have been working through some relatively minor injuries</a>, but both are healthy enough to play against the Eagles.</p><h3>Here are the Bears’ inactives:</h3><p>QB Caleb Williams (hamstring)<br>OT Ozzy Trapilo<br>OL Jordan McFadden<br>DL Jamree Kromah<br>DL Jayden Loving</p>

entries.title: New Bulls center Nic Claxton clears the air on back issues narrative
entries.summary: <p>Trying to change a narrative isn’t always easy, especially an NBA narrative.</p><p>Nic Claxton took his shot on Monday.</p><p>When the Bulls acquired the big man from Brooklyn, he came with a “handle with care” sign on his back, referring to the reported back issues he had been dealing with the previous two seasons.</p><p>After all, Claxton looked to be an up-and-comer during the 2022-23 season, averaging 12.6 points, 9.2 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game and then followed that up with a 2023-24 campaign of 11.8 points, 9.9 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game.</p><p>Then it dipped.</p><p>The scoring dropped to just over 10 per game, the rebounds down to 7.4 and the blocks 1.4. That’s also when the back flared up and made life tough for the center – for a year. That’s what he wanted to clear up during the Bulls’ media day.</p><p>Yes, he had a back issue during the 2024-25 season, but last year was more about Brooklyn in tank mode and messing with his minutes to make sure the mission to drop in the standings was carried out correctly.</p><p>“A couple years ago it really bothered me but last year it wasn’t a problem,” Claxton said. “It’s not a problem, now. I figured out my body, figured out what I need to do to stay on top of it, so I’m good to go.”</p><p>So what was last season?</p><p>Tanking 101</p><p>“Obviously yeah,” Claxton said, when asked if tanking can mess with a player’s game. “Especially last year, you prepare. You prepare to be the best version of yourself every single night and sometimes if your minutes are cut or the organization has a different agenda it can affect you. But at the end of the day, I’ve got to be a professional and be the best version of myself. I had a great time in Brooklyn and I’m excited to be here in Chicago.”</p><p>That’s because he knew his time with the Nets was basically over.</p><p>“I was in Brooklyn for seven years, so this is my first time being in a new city, meeting new media members, so it’s fun for me,” Claxton said. “It’s a little bit of an uncomfortable situation but I know it’s going to bring out the best in me. As far as the trade, I expected something to happen. It was time. It was time for both sides to move on.”</p><p></p><p><b>Off and running</b></p><p></p><p>Josh Giddey underwent arthroscopic surgery to repair a lingering right ankle issue last May and confirmed on Monday that he had been cleared for full-go runs and practices since the start of the month.</p><p>Good news for the point guard because with high-flying athletic wings like Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis, both tires need to be working.</p><p>“I think it’s my job to put guys in position to be successful,” Giddey said. “We’ve got a lot of different weapons, whether it’s Claxton a lob threat, we’ve got Norm (Normal Powell) who can shoot the ball from anywhere, we’ve got big wings that are elite in transition in Matas and Caleb.</p><p>“These guys (Buzelis and Wilson) are obviously elite getting downhill in transition, both extreme athletes that can get above the rim, so it’s kind of a point guard’s dream to have those guys running the wing and kicking it ahead to them.”</p><p></p><p><b>Being cautious</b></p><p></p><p>According to coach Tiago Splitter, the only Bulls player on the roster that might not be ready for a full day of practice with fall camp opening up on Tuesday was Zach Collins. The reserve center is dealing with a “soft tissue” issue that could slow him down at the start.</p>

entries.title: Analyzing Blackhawks' surprising lines, pairings to open season
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> coach Jeff Blashill pulled a surprise Monday — in the team's final practice before their season opener Tuesday — by mixing up the top three forward lines.</p><p>It's a bold move, considering he deployed a different set of lines consistently throughout training camp.</p><p>"Ultimately, we hadn't gotten enough out of the three lines with the combinations we had used," Blashill said.</p><p>He added he's not too concerned about the lack of practice time with these new lines, which were seemingly influenced by the Hawks' <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/26/blackhawks-anton-frondell-a-game-preseason-blues-sacha-boisvert" >solid performance</a> in their preseason finale Saturday.</p><p>But the trios will be immediately put to a steep test on the road in the opener Tuesday against the Golden Knights. Here's how the Hawks will take the ice in Las Vegas:</p><h3><b>Forward lines</b></h3><h3></h3><p><b>Oliver Moore — Roman Kantserov — Patrick Kane</b></p><p>Kantserov convinced Blashill on Saturday that he can play center in the NHL, which freed up Blashill — looking to spread out the Hawks' offensive playmakers over three lines instead of just two — to move Frank Nazar onto his own line.</p><p>Considering both Kantserov and Anton Frondell played on the wings for their European teams last season, though, it's quite daring to start this NHL season with both of them at center.</p><p>Moore has made it clear he prefers to play center, but it's becoming clear Blashill believes Moore's speedy style is better suited on the wing. He was turnover-prone in the preseason, so Blashill called on him to "make sure there's intent with every play."</p><p>Kane will be the Hawks' main attraction until Connor Bedard returns, and there's no question about his role.</p><p><b>Tyler Bertuzzi — Anton Frondell — Andrew Mangiapane</b></p><p>Bertuzzi and Frondell skated together throughout camp after some initial success last spring, when the Hawks outscored opponents 8-3 during their 109 minutes together.</p><p>Mangiapane only took Nick Lardis' spot on their right wing Saturday, though, with Blashill saying he thinks Mangiapane's north-south style and puck-pursuit eagerness matches Bertuzzi and Frondell better.</p><p>Teuvo Teravainen has rotated with Mangiapane, and Blashill insisted Monday he hasn't decided which of the two will dress Tuesday.</p><p><b>Ryan Donato — Frank Nazar — Nick Lardis</b></p><p>Blashill has raved about the Hawks' improved depth this season, but they'll need consistent production from both Frondell and Nazar's lines to keep up with contenders. </p><p>Time will tell how viable that is. This line, in particular, is a wild card. Nazar did have decent numbers with Lardis and with Donato (separately) last season.</p><p>Lardis stood out in camp practices but not as much in preseason games. Donato struggled in the preseason, but he deserves some benefit of the doubt after burying 46 goals over the last two seasons combined. </p><p><b>Cole Smith — Ryan Greene — Jordan Greenway</b></p><p>Blashill sounds very confident in this line, which has been a constant aside from Greenway's brief injury absence. </p><p>With two big grinders flanking Greene and his high hockey IQ, they'll be asked to create some ugly offense and, more importantly, take on tough defensive matchups.</p><p>"It's a huge bonus as a coach," Blashill said. "You're not hiding that line. You're actually fine with them going out against anybody."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Just three months ago, Cole Smith was playing for a Stanley Cup with the Golden Knights. Tomorrow, he's back in Vegas to face them with the Blackhawks.<br><br>"[Oliver] Mooresy goes, 'God, it's been a long time since we played.' I was like, 'It doesn't feel like it's been that long!'"</p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2104648750698315809?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 28, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>Defensive pairings</b></h3><p><b>Alex Vlasic — Bowen Byram</b></p><p>The Hawks stuck with the same pairings throughout camp, so the defensemen will enter Tuesday with more chemistry.</p><p>Vlasic and Byram seem to complement each other perfectly and have a chance to be the Hawks' best top pairing in years, even with left-handed Byram playing his off side. The franchise's new cornerstone defenseman was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/22/blackhawks-bowen-byram-swagger-confidence-preseason" target="_blank" >really impressive</a> in the preseason.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/22/blackhawks-bowen-byram-swagger-confidence-preseason" >Bowen Byram’s innate confidence will allow him to play his style, handle pressure with Blackhawks</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p><b>Wyatt Kaiser — Artyom Levshunov</b></p><p>In theory, Kaiser and Levshunov make sense together. Kaiser is a loud, avid communicator on the ice, giving Levshunov the extra guidance he sometimes needs. </p><p>Kaiser's quickness and intelligence also make him relatively good at anticipating and covering for Levshunov despite his erratic decision-making.</p><p>But in reality, this duo struggled last season; the Hawks were outscored 30-10 during their 431 minutes together. They're getting a chance to produce better results this season.</p><p><b>Ian Cole — Sam Rinzel</b></p><p>Cole, assuming a Connor Murphy-like <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/09/26/blackhawks-ian-cole-nhl-landon-slaggert-jeff-blashill" >veteran role</a>, will be tasked with stabilizing young Rinzel. Rinzel praised Cole for his tight gaps, overall calmness and ability to put him in spots to effectively utilize his skating and offensive inclinations.</p><p>"You don't realize how good he is until you play with him," Rinzel said.</p><p>Meanwhile, Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro — who skated as a fourth pairing throughout camp — both made the opening roster because the Hawks didn't want to risk losing either on waivers. </p><p>But playing time could be scarce for them. Blashill said he doesn't plan to deploy any seven-defensemen lineups or to regularly rotate the six defensemen in the lineup.</p><p>In goal, Spencer Knight will likely start Tuesday, with Arvid Soderblom likely getting his first start later on the road trip (in Utah or Buffalo).</p><p><b>Note: </b>Forward Landon Slaggert went unclaimed on waivers Monday and will start the season in Rockford.</p>

entries.title: Guardia de seguridad es grabado golpeando con su vehículo a muchacho en el ya cerrado Ford City Mall
entries.summary: <p>Un guardia de seguridad del ahora cerrado Ford City Mall ha sido acusado de atropellar a un muchacho de 18 años con su vehículo la noche del lunes pasado, luego de presuntamente agredir a su acompañante con una barra de metal en un incidente captado en video, según la Policía de Chicago.</p><p>Las víctimas —que hablaron con el Sun-Times bajo condición de anonimato— estaban montando patines eléctricos Lime en una acera cerca de la propiedad alrededor de las 11 p.m. cuando una camioneta SUV blanca se les acercó antes de que un hombre se bajara y buscara algo en el asiento trasero.</p><p>Uno de los conductores de los patines, un hombre de 28 años, intentó hablar con el guardia de seguridad, quien, sin decir palabra, presuntamente lo golpeó con un objeto de metal.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-c80000" name="module-c80000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>El muchacho de 18 años y el hombre de 28 entonces huyeron, mientras el guardia de seguridad no identificado los seguía en su vehículo. Finalmente los alcanzó y atropelló al más joven cerca de un gimnasio que opera dentro del centro comercial.</p><p>Paramédicos atendieron a ambos en la escena por lesiones, según la Policía de Chicago, que dijo que el caso sigue bajo investigación. No se han hecho arrestos.</p><p>“Nunca había tenido un enfrentamiento con seguridad así. Normalmente sólo te piden que te vayas, y nosotros obedecemos”, dijo el muchacho.</p><p>Los videos del encuentro, que han acumulado decenas de miles de vistas en distintas plataformas de redes sociales, muestran al conductor de una SUV blanca acelerando y golpeando al muchacho, lo que lo hace caer del patín eléctrico mientras graba. Ambos habían llevado cámaras GoPro y estaban grabando al momento del incidente.</p><p>En un comunicado, Namdar Realty Group, actual propietaria de Ford City Mall, dijo que estaba “perturbada por lo que parece mostrar” lo ocurrido en los videos.</p><p>“La seguridad de cualquier persona en nuestra propiedad, sin importar las circunstancias, es importante para nosotros, y las acciones mostradas no reflejan los protocolos de seguridad del centro comercial ni la conducta que la empresa propietaria aprueba”, señaló el comunicado. “Estamos tomando la investigación de este incidente muy en serio, en </div> </div></div><p>El concejal Derrick Curtis (18.º), cuyo distrito abarca la propiedad, dijo que anteriormente tuvo que presionar a la compañía para que contratara seguridad, aunque desde entonces Hay demasiada delincuencia”, dijo Curtis al Sun-Times el jueves. “[Pero] no sólo haremos responsable a la empresa de seguridad, sino también a Namdar, por todas las lesiones”.</p><p>Las víctimas se describen a sí mismos como exploradores urbanos, que a menudo graban videos en edificios abandonados y dentro de ellos en varias partes del mundo. Explicaron que esa noche sólo estaban conduciendo por el estacionamiento y que están acostumbrados a interactuar con seguridad, que por lo general solo les pide que se vayan.</p><p>En otros casos, la policía es llamada y se les emite una orden de no entrar.</p><p>Explicaron que la hostilidad los tomó por sorpresa, ya que sus interacciones con otros guardias de seguridad han sido relativamente cordiales porque “nuestro objetivo no es dañar ni hacer nada malo”.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="FacebookUrl"> <script>(function(d, s, id) { var js, fjs = d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0]; if (d.getElementById(id)) return; js = d.createElement(s); js.id = id; js.src = "//connect.facebook.net/en_US/sdk.js#xfbml=1&version=v20.0"; fjs.parentNode.insertBefore(js, fjs); }(document, 'script', 'facebook-jssdk'));</script><div class="fb-post" data-href="https://www.facebook.com/reel/842040575618386"></div> </div> </div> </div></div><p>“Que nos respondan con violencia es anormal. No es lo que suele hacer la seguridad”, dijo el hombre de 28 años, quien prefirió no ser identificado y publica contenido bajo las cuentas de redes sociales DecayingMidwest. “Hay que hacer algo. Simplemente no quiero que alguien muera”.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" >La Voz Chicago</a><br></p>

entries.title: Bulls willing to temper excitement around rookie Caleb Wilson
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" target="_blank" >Bulls</a> executive vice president of basketball operations Bryson Graham was knee-deep in the circus Monday.</p><p>After all, that’s what most NBA media days are. Take pictures here, cut a scream clip for the hometown scoreboard there, pose with this teammate back there, dribble the ball for this camera here.</p><p>A complete circus.</p><p>But through the monotony of the afternoon, something across the atrium suddenly caught Graham’s eye.</p><p>‘‘He was standing next to [coach] Tiago [Splitter],’’ Graham said of star rookie Caleb Wilson. ‘‘They were taking pictures.’’</p><p>Graham then turned to Splitter at the media table.</p><p>‘‘He was looking at you eye-to-eye, bro,’’ Graham told Splitter. ‘‘What are you, 6-11?’’</p><p>‘‘Six-10½,’’ Splitter responded.</p><p>‘‘[Wilson is] 6-10½ and multipositional, versatile,’’ Graham said. ‘‘He tries to make the right play. Not one day during these pickup games — this is what has been so exciting — has he come out and said, ‘I’m going to shoot every time.’ He’s still trying to make the right play. That’s just who he is. Nothing has slapped him down. It’s going to be hard to do that because he’s a competitive kid and has very big aspirations.’’</p><p>Since announcing his arrival to the NBA with a 35-point performance in his Summer League debut in July, Wilson — the No. 4 overall pick in the draft — has been tested with workouts and open scrimmages against NBA players and has yet to blink.</p><p>If anything, he continues to show the Bulls that something special has, in fact, arrived.</p><p>‘‘Just like everybody in this room, we’re excited about Caleb,’’ Splitter said. ‘‘He’s a No. 4 pick, and every day he’s showing us why he’s the No. 4 pick. Also, it’s really hard to put him on a floor or with a ceiling, to be honest. We’re going to help him be the best player he can be. What that is, we don’t know.’’</p><p>The feeling, however, is that Wilson eventually will be a foundation-changer.</p><p>‘‘The expectations are probably pretty high because Caleb is pretty outspoken, but internally we know it’s a season of growth and development,’’ Graham said. ‘‘We have to be OK with giving him grace this year because he’s going to have some ups and downs. There’s going to be progress, and there’s going to be some regression.”</p><p>That’s a reality even the ever-confident Wilson knows awaits him.</p><p>What Wilson has on his side, however, is an impressive work ethic that has the coaching staff reminding him to go home at night, rather than staying too late in the practice facility.</p><p>Wilson does that to get better and to show his teammates how committed he is to helping the Bulls rebuild.</p><p>‘‘I feel like, as a rookie, people respect action more than they respect words,’’ Wilson said. ‘‘I’ll let my actions lead, and eventually I’ll blend in talking. But my whole goal is letting everyone know what the tone is by showing what I’m going to do. That’s how I’ve always led.</p><p>‘‘I won’t say where I fit in right now. I feel like, as a player, I’m going to be very important to our future and what we’re doing now. So I just go out there and let it happen.’’</p>

entries.title: Ford City Mall security guard suspended after viral video shows him hitting teen with car
entries.summary: <p>A security guard working for the owners of Ford City Mall has been placed on indefinite leave after elected officials called for accountability following a viral video showing the man <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/24/ald-curtis-calls-for-accountability-after-security-vehicle-strikes-teen-at-ford-city-mall" target="_blank" ><u>hitting a teen with his car</u></a>.</p><p>The guard is suspended indefinitely “pending the outcome of the ongoing investigation into the incident, which is being conducted in continued collaboration with the Chicago Police Department,” according to a statement from the mall’s ownership.</p><p>No arrests have been made and no charges have been filed, though an investigation is ongoing, according to Chicago police.</p><p>Dashboard-mounted cameras have also been added to security vehicles “to provide additional documentation and accountability going forward."</p><p>“Ownership has also since re-reviewed the existing protocols and expectations with the full security team around not engaging with trespassers, involving law enforcement, and the prohibited use of personal vehicles while on-duty,” the statement said.</p><p>The victims — who previously spoke to the Chicago Sun-Times on condition of anonymity — said they were riding Lime e-scooters on a sidewalk near the property around 11 p.m. last
